div.head: ECf 32 E 5
div.ab: Occupauerunt uero Norwegienses terras multas et insulas regni huius, quas adhuc detinent occupatas: non potuerunt unquam postea penitus euelli nec expelli. Tandem modo confederati sunt nobis in regno fide et sacramento et per uxores suas, quas postea ceperunt de sanguine nostro, et per affinitates et per coniugia.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 660 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 E …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
div.ab: And the Norwegians occupied many lands and islands of this kingdom, which they still hold occupied: they could never afterwards be wholly uprooted or expelled. At last they are now bound to us in the kingdom by faith and oath, and through their wives, whom they afterwards took from our blood, and through affinities and through marriages.
